title: whatsapp sessions._id (= bare hash of groupJid:ownerUserId) and its turns._id (sha256 of sessionId:messageId) are still not tenant-scoped
evidence: apps/api/src/whatsapp/store.ts used sessionId = source._id; with the source _id now tenant-scoped the session id is kept as the bare source.hash so chunks/claims/evidence/citations (which cite sessionId) and the turn ids (derived from sessionId, messageId not stored on the turn so they cannot be recomputed in a migration) do not change. sessions._id therefore stays globally unique across tenants for whatsapp. The owner id is bound to one tenant, so a real collision needs the same groupJid and ownerUserId under two tenants.
fix_direction: Approver decision: whether session ids are public identifiers (citations, URLs) and may be rewritten; if yes, a second migration must rewrite sessions._id, turns.sessionId, turns._id (needs messageId), chunks.sourceRef, claims/decisions/session_pages/speakers evidence.sessionId, tree_index sessionRef.

title: migration test never exercises media.sourceRef updateMany: mutant deleting it survives
evidence: Mutation M3 (comment out reference('media','sourceRef')) -> migration tests 11/11 pass. Fixture media rows are all `${old}-media`, which the rename loop rewrites anyway. A media row with another _id shape (evidence clip) and sourceRef=bare id would be uncovered by tests (production code is correct).
fix_direction: Add a media fixture whose _id is not `${old}-media` with sourceRef=old; file-don't-fix unless the migration is next touched.

title: migration scale: sources.find({}).toArray() unbatched; gaps.sourceRef has no index; owner map allows one owner under two tenants
evidence: migrate() loads every sources doc (and each journal doc embeds the full row) in one array and does ~8 round trips per row; gaps.updateMany({tenantId, sourceRef}) has no supporting index. createConfiguredWhatsAppOwnerResolver does not reject one ownerUserId mapped to two tenants, which is the only way ISS-TENANTSRCID-001 collides.
fix_direction: Use a cursor and batch before the real-DB run; validate owner-map uniqueness. Not blocking.
